rationale: This is essentially a rank-multiplied double sort on two well-published anomalies (R&D-to-sales, Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, and Sloan accruals) with no mechanism that is not already spanned by their separate main effects, so the "interaction" adds little beyond a composite of known signals.

The advertising-intensity-growth leg is a less-mined ingredient and the sign convention on NEG(Δwcap/at) is internally consistent with the accrual anomaly, though the second leg is basically balance-sheet Sloan and xad's sparse reporting will likely make coverage and portfolio composition unstable.

Zero-filling all non-goodwill-growers via INDICATOR creates a large point mass that will dominate the cross-sectional sort and portfolio breakpoints, and what remains is the standard accrual anomaly conditioned on M&A activity — a documented conditioning, not a new mechanism.

The denominator ADD(ABS(accruals),ABS(dp/at)) is dominated by depreciation intensity rather than "accrual noise," so the signal is effectively an intangibles-to-depreciation ratio with explosive values when the denominator is near zero, and the stated hypothesis does not match what is computed.

Smoothed R&D intensity interacted with accrual-volatility (an earnings-quality/idiosyncratic-risk proxy) is a coherent and directionally consistent construction, but it remains close to a composite of two known effects and the 5-period VOL plus xrd requirement will thin coverage materially.

Compustat recch/invch are signed as cash-flow sources (positive = receivables/inventory decrease), so NEG(recch+invch) rewards exactly the accrual buildup the hypothesis claims to penalize — a direct sign inconsistency — compounded by requiring xrd, xad, recch and invch jointly, which will leave very sparse coverage.
